threads.body: [General] This changes legacy/default telemetry despite the PR stating it is unchanged. Previously this getter always returned the cached `GeodeServerAddress`, and `DbClientAttributesExtractor` invokes the server extractor in every database semconv mode; returning `null` here therefore removes the existing `server.address`/`server.port` from default-mode spans (as the updated default test expectations also show). Preserve the old address path for old-only mode, while using `GeodeServerTarget` for modes that emit stable database conventions.

replies.body:
Addressed in f200677a9f934e75f3d4a01e3199de8317f11aed.

Analysis: The default mode must keep resolving one configured server through the per-region `GeodeServerAddress` cache. Stable mode must use `GeodeServerTarget` so it can report the configured server, locator, or group target.

Upsides: Existing default-mode `server.address` and `server.port` telemetry stays compatible, while stable mode keeps the richer configured-target behavior.

Downsides: The agent retains the legacy address helper and its cached pool lookup for default mode.

Addressed in b89e844079df5f04440225d6348027d5eed59727.

Analysis: Both classes are implementation details used only inside the Geode instrumentation package. Package-private visibility matches the neighboring Geode classes and still permits the same-package unit test and instrumentation module to use them.

Upsides: The javaagent module exposes fewer implementation types and follows the repository's least-access rule.

Downsides: No material downside identified.

threads.body: [Style] All callers of this helper are in the same instrumentation package, so public visibility is broader than necessary. Keep the helper package-private like the existing Geode helpers.

replies.body:
No code change.

Analysis: The advice methods directly call `GeodeServerTargets` after Byte Buddy applies them to Geode classes in other packages. Repository guidance requires classes and methods directly referenced from advice to remain public because the agent can override the advice inlining mode at runtime.

Upsides: Keeping the helper public prevents access errors in transformed Geode classes across all advice dispatch modes.

Downsides: The helper remains publicly visible inside the javaagent artifact.
